title: Curcuma longa reduces microphthalmia-associated transcription factor expression – Journal of Pharmacy & Pharmacognosy Research
abstract:
# *Curcuma longa* L. (*Zingiberaceae*) extract protects against epithelial damage and reduces the expression of the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor in UVB-exposed Wistar rats  
## \[El extracto de *Curcuma longa* L. (*Zingiberaceae*) protege contra el daño epitelial y reduce la expresión del factor de transcripción asociado a la microftalmia en ratas Wistar expuestas a la radiación UVB]  
### Deni Firmansyah1,2, Sri Adi Sumiwi3, Nyi Mekar Saptarini4, Jutti Levita3*  
1Doctoral Program in Pharmacy, Faculty of Pharmacy, Padjadjaran University, Sumedang 45363, Indonesia.  
2Department of Pharmacology, Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Muhammadiyah Ahmad Dahlan Cirebon, Cirebon 45153, Indonesia.  
3Department of Pharmacology and Clinical Pharmacy, Faculty of Pharmacy, Padjadjaran University, Sumedang 46363, Indonesia.  
4Department of Pharmaceutical Analysis and Medicinal Chemistry, Faculty of Pharmacy, Padjadjaran University, Sumedang 46363, Indonesia.  
\*E-mail: [jutti.levita@unpad.ac.id](https://jppres.com/jppres/curcuma-longa-reduces-microphthalmia-associated-transcription-factor-expression/mailto:jutti.levita@unpad.ac.id)  
**Abstract**
*Conclusions*: *Curcuma longa* extract could be considered a potential candidate for a skincare product, but further clinical studies are needed to verify its efficacy and safety.  
*Keywords*: curcuminoids; melanogenesis; MITF; skincare; turmeric; tyrosinase; *Zingiberaceae*.
